findings.explanation: Splunkbase 1546 is the community 'REST API Modular Input' (rest_ta), not a Splunk-built 'Splunk Add-on for REST'. The wrong name sends readers looking for a Splunk-supported add-on that does not exist. The same error appears in implementation, detailedImplementation and references.
findings.suggested_fix: Call it 'REST API Modular Input (Splunkbase 1546, rest_ta)' everywhere, and note its support model, or use a custom modular input or Add-on Builder input.

findings.explanation: Qualtrics response export is asynchronous. You POST to export-responses to get a progressId, poll the progress endpoint until it returns a fileId, then GET .../{fileId}/file, which is zipped by default. A plain periodic REST poll of this endpoint will not return response rows. The JSON excerpt in dataSources is also not the shape of a direct API reply.
findings.quote: configure modular inputs targeting Qualtrics REST API v3 survey-response exports (`/API/v3/surveys/{surveyId}/export-responses`) ... poll every fifteen minutes
findings.suggested_fix: Describe the three-step export (start, poll progress, download the file with `compress:false` or unzip) with an incremental `startDate` or continuation token, implemented as a custom scripted or modular input rather than a single REST poll.

findings.explanation: props.conf forbids KV_MODE=json together with INDEXED_EXTRACTIONS=json because fields are extracted twice. TIMESTAMP_FIELDS lists the fields that together make up one timestamp, not alternative fields per vendor. INDEXED_EXTRACTIONS also does not apply to HEC /services/collector/event payloads, which are the main webhook path here. The same stanza is repeated in detailedImplementation, alongside TIME_PREFIX.
findings.suggested_fix: Use one stanza per vendor sourcetype with a single timestamp field. Pair INDEXED_EXTRACTIONS=json with KV_MODE=none (file/UF ingest only), or use KV_MODE=json alone for HEC event data and set the timestamp via the HEC `time` field.

findings.explanation: Every cross-reference points to an unrelated UC. UC-23.4.6 is Internal Mobility & Promotion Velocity, UC-23.5.6 is Production Throughput vs Forecast Capacity, and UC-23.7.3 is Customer Effort Score and Support Channel Effectiveness, which is customer CES, not eNPS. UC-23.1.5 is attribution, not consent telemetry.
findings.quote: Operational call-centre QA scoring (Verint Speech Analytics) tracked separately in UC-23.4.6. Vendor-NPS for partner / supplier programmes excluded (UC-23.5.6). Internal employee NPS (eNPS) is monitored in UC-23.7.3
findings.suggested_fix: Remove the UC IDs or replace them with the UCs that actually cover call-centre QA, supplier NPS and eNPS. Note that UC-23.7.3 overlaps this UC's CES metric.

findings.explanation: Those are per-response bucketing rules, not the alert. The SPL's `where` clause fires on a weekly NPS move of more than 5 points with at least 50 responses, CSAT below 80% with more than 100 CSAT responses, any detractor on a major-incident day, or post-launch NPS below the benchmark floor. The description also names only `qualtrics:survey_export`, while seven sourcetypes are searched.
findings.suggested_fix: Rewrite the description around the weekly product × channel grain and the four alert conditions with their thresholds.

findings.explanation: The four listed scenarios are generic and nonsensical for survey data (synthetic probes, batch `sum`, CMDB CHG maintenance). Meanwhile detailedImplementation Step 5 has 19 real interpretation hazards: survey fatigue, thin strata, translation distortion, incentive pushes, scale mixing.
findings.quote: Synthetic probe on `_time`, `product`, `contact_channel` — Health checks in `cx_voc_responses` populate the same fields
findings.suggested_fix: Replace the field with the strongest Step 5 hazards (thin strata under 50 responses, channel mix shift, Likert wording changes, incident overlays, star-to-NPS scale mixing), each with its mitigation.

findings.explanation: The 0-10 eleven-point scale is NPS. The SPL treats CSAT as 5- or 7-point (top-two-box), so this sentence contradicts the search logic.
findings.quote: so CES seven-point scales separate cleanly from eleven-point CSAT scales
findings.suggested_fix: Say: separate 0-10 NPS, 5/7-point CSAT and 7-point CES scales.

findings.explanation: Neither the Qualtrics webhook signature header name nor a 'Webhooks v2' SurveyMonkey product could be confirmed. SurveyMonkey webhooks are part of API v3. A Heavy Forwarder Python shim is also not available on Splunk Cloud HEC.
findings.quote: validating `X-Qualtrics-Signature` HMAC-SHA256 against shared secrets ... SurveyMonkey Webhooks v2
findings.suggested_fix: Check the Qualtrics event-subscription documentation for the actual signing mechanism and the SurveyMonkey v3 webhook documentation. Describe a supported signature-validation tier (for example, an API gateway in front of HEC).

findings.explanation: Much of the ingest prose is dense keyword chaining that gives no concrete steps (endpoints, auth, sourcetype mapping), especially Paths C-G and the Step 3 validation list.
findings.quote: Path E — InMoment XI hourly pulls unify legacy Wootric microsurvey intervals plus Allegiance Engage batches.
findings.suggested_fix: For each vendor path, give the endpoint, auth method, input type, sourcetype and timestamp field in a short table.

findings.explanation: The SOAR playbook, the saved-search name and `evidence_index` appear nowhere else in the UC. Implementation and detailedImplementation route to Teams/Slack and Salesforce, not SOAR.
findings.quote: routed via SOAR `cx_voc_remediation_v2` execution log ... `| rest /services/saved/searches/cx_voc_nps_drop_alert_v3`
findings.suggested_fix: Use the saved-search name and routing actually described in Step 4, and drop the SOAR artefact unless a playbook is part of the build.

findings.explanation: The closing clause is garbled. The explanation also says 'star ratings', while the core metrics are NPS (0-10) and CSAT surveys.
findings.quote: and raise the alarm before renewals turn hostile—not before counting clicks or carts alone.
findings.suggested_fix: e.g. 'We collect customers' survey scores and comments, track each week whether satisfaction is rising or falling for each product and channel, and warn the team when it drops sharply or right after an outage or launch.'

findings.explanation: The reviewer is an authoring agent, not an SME, and the add-on name, Qualtrics API flow and props errors show the content was not verified.
findings.suggested_fix: Set the status to draft/community until a human CX or Splunk reviewer validates it.

firewalled_field_flags.issue: `coalesce(customer_id_pii_hash,customer_hash,account_hash,acct_h_77,"")` uses a sample data value (`acct_h_77`) as a field name. SurveyMonkey's `custom_value` is never mapped.
`strptime(recordedDate,"%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S.%3NZ")` will not parse the sample `2024-09-15T14:30:00Z`, which has no milliseconds, so it silently falls back to `_time`.

`sum(incident_hit)` counts responses on incident days, not incident days. `correlated_to_incident` fires on any single detractor during an incident, which makes this condition very noisy. `wilson_margin` is calculated but never used and is not a Wilson interval. `sort _time` without 0 truncates at 10,000 rows.

summary: The UC has rich, VOC-specific material (multi-vendor ingest paths and a strong list of interpretation hazards). But it misnames the Splunkbase 1546 add-on and gives an ingest recipe that would not work: a single GET on Qualtrics' asynchronous export API, plus invalid props.conf settings. The description misstates the alert logic, and every exclusion cross-reference points to the wrong UC.
